action.purpose: SwiftUI body semibold; native semantic sizing.

control.purpose: SwiftUI callout medium; native semantic sizing.

countdown.purpose: System rounded light numerals with monospaced digits in TimerActivityView.

duration.purpose: System rounded light hours and minutes with monospaced digits in DurationEditor.

end-time.purpose: Editable native NSDatePicker in NativeTimePicker, using the plain 38-point light AppKit system font with locale-aware hour/minute segments. Unlike countdown and duration numerals, this control does not use the rounded display font or a separate read-only clock.

motion.name: switch-state
motion.purpose: AwakeGlassToggleStyle state transition, including its native glass thumb between x: −11 and +11 points. No explicit animation with Reduce Motion; native switch fallback for Reduce Transparency or macOS before 26.

motion.name: session-selection
motion.purpose: SessionModePicker animates only the horizontal offset of one persistent regular-glass capsule on macOS 26+, with zero vertical offset. Labels remain stationary above the glass container; the track stays 44 points high. Mode-specific editors, notices, and surrounding panel content do not animate. No explicit animation with Reduce Motion; native segmented Picker on earlier macOS. The horizontal-only trajectory is constrained in source, without video-frame verification.

components.name: Primary action
components.description: Schematic action preview. SessionSetupView and TimerActivityView call awakeGlassButton(prominent: true); native accent-tinted glass and platform interaction states are authoritative.

components.name: Secondary action
components.description: Schematic +15 min action preview. The native source uses awakeGlassButton(), a capsule border shape, and callout medium text.

components.name: Selected duration preset
components.description: Schematic selected preset. DurationEditor presents six ordinary buttons in a three-column grid and marks the matching duration as selected; this is a value shortcut, not a filter.

components.name: Duration field
components.description: Schematic numeric field with one CSS pixel per native logical point. DurationEditor uses a 96 × 58 point plain SwiftUI TextField, system rounded light type, and monospaced digits; its parser remains authoritative.

components.name: Until time editor
components.description: Schematic editable-clock preview; the native NSDatePicker and its keyboard segments, locale-aware AM/PM, and stepper are authoritative. SessionEndTimeEditor uses one transparent, borderless 38-point light system-font clock, a secondary Today/Tomorrow and relative-duration summary, and three secondary glass shortcuts. Calendar-based next-occurrence selection handles passed clock times; the 24-hour guard remains enforced. This static preview does not implement calendar logic or reproduce native glass.

components.name: Session mode picker
components.description: Schematic selection preview. On macOS 26+, SessionModePicker slides one persistent 36-point regular-glass capsule horizontally beneath stationary native button labels overlaid after GlassEffectContainer. Buttons are 36 points high with 4-point gaps/insets in a fixed 44-point track. Only the capsule x offset uses 0.25-second smooth motion, with zero vertical offset and no changing glass effect identities; Reduce Motion omits the animation. Editors and panel content do not animate. Earlier macOS uses a native segmented Picker. Live selection and accessibility selected state were verified, with readable labels and an aligned track in Timer/Unlimited captures; motion was not video-frame verified. Native rendering and semantics are authoritative.

components.name: Closed-lid status card
components.description: Schematic geometry and copy preview. ClosedLidControl uses native regular glass (regularMaterial before macOS 26), 16-point insets and 20-point continuous corners. Unconfirmed status and warnings use secondary gray; confirmed protection uses green. Status precedence is issue, confirmed active, checking, approval, setup, off, then starting/ready. Transport or update failures offer Repair helper without implying readiness. This neutral Off example makes no protection claim; actual success requires its confirmed predicate.

components.name: Glass switch
components.description: Schematic proportions only: 52 × 30 point capsule track and 24-point native glass thumb with horizontal offsets −11/+11. AwakeGlassToggleStyle owns native keyboard activation, a single named accessibility toggle with guarded action, disabled opacity, 0.22-second smooth state transition, and Reduce Motion handling. Older macOS or Reduce Transparency uses a native switch. The HTML preview uses a checkbox for operable semantics; it does not reproduce Apple glass.

components.name: Settings glass section
components.description: Schematic SettingsGlassSection geometry: header above content with 10-point spacing, 20-point continuous glass corners, 16-point content inset, 12-point row spacing and optional wrapping detail. SettingsScrollPage supplies 24-point page insets and 22-point section gaps. License cards share the inset and glass treatment. Native regular glass or the regularMaterial fallback is authoritative. Its SettingsView host uses a text-only native General / Closed Lid / License segmented picker in the actual toolbar, with unified compact system-height chrome and no repeated heading or oversized icons. A narrow AppKit anchor applies only toolbar style and hidden title visibility, including on macOS 14; the logical Untiring Settings title and traffic lights remain. Pages stay mounted to preserve drafts and scroll state, with hidden pages disabled, excluded from hit testing, and hidden from accessibility. Older-system rendering and full keyboard/accessibility coverage remain unverified.

narrative.overview:
A compact, calm control panel built from SwiftUI system controls, adaptive materials, SF Symbols, and clear status copy. Large, light numerals give the session its focus; glass capsules and a dedicated protection card keep actions and readiness easy to distinguish.

This records the shared menu-bar, Settings, and license activation system. Compact native Settings navigation leads to scrollable glass sections with concise labels; switches and session selection carry the same iOS-like control feel. Native SwiftUI rendering is authoritative: the sidecar's HTML previews are schematic references, not reproductions of Apple's glass renderer. Dimensions above are macOS logical points; system fonts resolve through the platform rather than bundled font files.
keyCharacteristics: System typography with light, rounded session numerals.
Adaptive glass sections, capsule actions, and glass switch thumbs.
Compact composition with scrollable settings and fully wrapping status details.
Text, symbols, and semantic color convey protection state together.

rules.name: The Confirmation Rule
rules.body: Green protection status accompanies a confirmed helper state and explicit success copy; selecting the switch or starting a session alone cannot produce it.

rules.name: The Native Material Rule
rules.body: Reuse the availability-aware glass helpers; do not replace adaptive system rendering with fixed blur, painted highlights, or screenshot-derived colors.

dos: Do reuse the native glass helpers and semantic text styles.
Do keep session controls and closed-lid confirmation visually distinct.
Do retain complete wrapping status and error explanations.
Do preserve native control semantics, keyboard actions, and accessible names.
Do respect Reduce Motion and keep the native switch fallback for Reduce Transparency and older macOS.
Do scope explicit state animation to switches and the session selector, leaving panel content changes unanimated.
donts: Don't infer protection from a running countdown or an enabled switch.
Don't hard-code colors sampled from one wallpaper, appearance, or OS version.
Don't introduce a second custom glass, shadow, or animation system for these surfaces.
